children: is facing fresh skepticism over whether it can hit its long-term growth targets, with Argus downgrading the restaurant operator to Hold from Buy as food-safety fallout, softer comparable sales and margin pressure weigh on the outlook. The call puts particular focus on whether Yum can still deliver at least 8% core operating profit growth while navigating near-term weakness at Taco Bell and KFC.

Yum owns major restaurant chains including Taco Bell, KFC and Pizza Hut, with a heavily franchised model that generates revenue through franchise fees, royalties and company-operated stores. That structure has historically supported relatively resilient margins and capital-light growth.

Argus analyst John Staszak said the company's long-term algorithm of 5% annual unit growth, 7% system sales growth and at least 8% core operating profit growth looks increasingly difficult to achieve over the next several quarters.

We think these targets will be difficult to achieve over the next few quarters as food-safety issues at Taco Bell, promotional efforts, and low-single-digit comp growth at KFC, among other factors, to pressure earnings, Staszak wrote.

He cut his fiscal 2026 EPS estimate to $6.40 from $7, implying roughly 6% growth and sitting close to the $6.39 consensus. For 2027, he reduced his preliminary adjusted EPS forecast to $7.00 from $7.80.
Margins are also under pressure. Yum's second-quarter operating margin fell to 30.7% from 32.2% a year earlier, while company restaurant expenses increased.
One potential offset is the planned sale of U.S. Pizza Hut restaurants this quarter, which could remove a drag on results and let management focus more heavily on KFC and Taco Bell.

title: Analyst Revamps Yum Stock Target on Major Risk
